## FOLLICULITIS
Folliculitis is an infection of the hair follicle with purulent exudate in the
epidermis. It is usually associated with Staphylococcus aureus. In patients
exposed to swimming pools or hot tubs, folliculitis may be associated with
Pseudomonas aeruginosa. Candida albicans can cause folliculitis in patients
receiving antimicrobials and/or corticosteroids. For folliculitis in patients
with severe acne, consult Dermatology. For extensive folliculitis or in
patients with HIV, consult Infectious Diseases.
## Treatment
Usually self-limiting. For most cases, treat with daily saline compresses until
symptoms resolve.
## Inpatient

## For moderate to severe cases associated with Staphylococcus aureus:
Mupirocin ointment to affected area q8h for 7 days ($) [M]
## For cases associated with Candida albicans
Clotrimazole cream q8h for 7 days ($) [M]
## Outpatient

## For moderate to severe cases associated with Staphylococcus aureus:
Mupirocin 2% ointment topical to affected area TID for 7 days ($) [M]
Non-VA order for above
## For cases associated with Candida albicans
Clotrimazole cream to affected area TID for 7 days ($) [M]
Non-VA order for above
